chain.label: High density altitude from 34-41 C ambient temperatures at 4,000-5,300 ft, leaving only a marginal out-of-ground-effect hover and 41-421 fpm vertical climb margin
chain.trigger: no evidence of any meteorological phenomenon that was contributory to the accident other than the high-ambient temperatures and resultant high-density altitude

chain.label: Precipitous Grand Wash Cliffs escarpment with a rocky 40-degree slope immediately below the route
chain.trigger: Passing over the cliff edge along this route, the terrain drops off dramatically to barren desert floor 3,000 feet below

chain.label: 5 to 10 knot westerly wind, which became a tailwind once the helicopter reversed to an easterly heading into the cliff
chain.trigger: an alert and proficient pilot would never intentionally turn the helicopter toward any type of sloping terrain, especially one that would expose the helicopter to a 5- to 10-knot tailwind

chain.label: FAA policy required no direct en route surveillance of air tour flights operating outside the SFAR airspace
chain.trigger: FAA's local and national policy did not contain adequate guidance or requirements for direct surveillance of thousands of air tour flights that occur outside of the SFAR

chain.label: Pilot's established practice of crossing the cliff edge low and fast and then diving the helicopter over the rim to entertain passengers
chain.trigger: he preferred to cross the cliff edge at low altitude and high speed... he would then enter a rapid descent by lowering the collective and nosing the helicopter over into a dive

caused_by.evidence: there is no requirement for him to perform direct (in-flight) surveillance of Papillon's tour routes outside the airspace designed by the SFAR... none was performed

chain.label: Pilot's decision to maneuver the helicopter into a flight regime that sharply reduced its available performance margin
chain.trigger: a probable scenario involves the pilot's decision to maneuver the helicopter in a flight regime, and in a high density altitude environment, which significantly decreased the helicopter's performance capability

caused_by.evidence: Several of the operator's tour pilots, including the accident pilot, nicknamed this maneuver the Thelma and Louise descent
the criticality of the high-density altitude and the helicopter's weight... the helicopter would have had only a marginal capability to slow to zero airspeed at the ridgeline elevation

chain.label: Helicopter operating below the cliff rim in close proximity to the escarpment, with little altitude available for recovery
chain.trigger: This maneuver would have placed the helicopter below the cliff edge, facing into the escarpment

caused_by.evidence: the accident helicopter passed over the cliff edge, and rather than continuing straight ahead along the route, the helicopter reduced forward airspeed and reversed its heading

chain.label: Abrupt reduction of forward airspeed below minimum-power airspeed and a descending 180-degree heading reversal back toward the cliff face
chain.trigger: the helicopter reduced forward airspeed and reversed its heading... a descending 180 degree turn with an abrupt slowing of forward speed back toward the cliff

caused_by.evidence: the pilot's decision to maneuver the helicopter in a flight regime... which significantly decreased the helicopter's performance capability

chain.label: High vertical rate of descent that exceeded the power available to arrest it, despite full-up collective and full-right antitorque pedal at impact
chain.trigger: resulting in a high rate of descent from which the pilot was unable to recover prior to ground impact

caused_by.evidence: any airspeed decrease below VY would require an increase in power; as the speed decreases toward zero, the power required to maintain altitude is just under or equal to the power required to HOGE or available from the engine
If the helicopter were descending vertically (or nearly so) at a greater rate [than 421 fpm], the pilot could not arrest the descent
any tailwind component would significantly decrease the hover and vertical climb performance capabilities of the helicopter
the high rate of descent occurred in proximity to precipitous terrain, which effectively limited remedial options available

chain.label: Helicopter struck a rocky 40-degree slope upright with insignificant forward velocity at an estimated 10 to 16 G, and was destroyed by impact and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: collided with terrain during an uncontrolled descent about 4 miles east of Meadview, Arizona... destroyed by impact forces and a postcrash fire

caused_by.evidence: there was insignificant forward velocity and a very high, vertical descent rate at impact
the helicopter came to rest in the least advantageous location available... a rocky 40 degree slope

chain.label: Pilot and five passengers fatally injured; remaining passenger seriously injured
chain.trigger: The pilot and five passengers were killed, and the remaining passenger sustained serious injuries

caused_by.evidence: The helicopter was destroyed by impact forces and a postcrash fire
